summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of chronic left shoulder pain due to rotator cuff tears, SIADH, and aortic stenosis was admitted for severe worsening shoulder pain and a low sodium level of 118. Evaluation revealed septic arthritis of the left shoulder caused by Streptococcus viridans, confirmed by joint fluid analysis. He underwent open irrigation and debridement and was started on intravenous vancomycin, with a PICC line placed for long-term antibiotic therapy. During the hospitalization, he developed transient atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, which resolved spontaneously; he was started on warfarin with a heparin bridge for stroke prevention. His hyponatremia, attributed to SIADH exacerbated by pain, improved with fluid restriction. He remained afebrile with decreasing white blood cell count and was discharged to extended care for completion of a four-week antibiotic course, ongoing anticoagulation management, and rehabilitation.
